_comment: This file is the ONE source. crypto-quant-signal-mcp reads it directly;
algovault-skills carries a VENDORED copy plus a committed .sha256 of THIS file,
and a parity assertion in each repo. The row below is the only canonical hash
reference point — the vendored copy never records a second hash of its own,
because a second recorded hash is a second thing that can drift.
WHY A PATTERN, NOT A LITERAL LIST: '20 calls/day', '20 free calls/day' and
'20 calls per day' are one class. A literal list lets '25 calls/day' through
tomorrow, which is exactly the defect this gate exists to make impossible.
WHY NO BRAND-FACTS PROSE: brand-facts.md is private (vault). Only the
machine-checkable pattern and a citation travel into this public repo — same
discipline as ops/claudemd-claims.lock.json, which carries identifiers only.
SCOPE: seeded with per-day-quota ONLY. This wave is not a brand-facts

exempt_paths.reason: The runbook that DOCUMENTS this ban has to quote the banned phrase to be useful ('Never write 20 calls/day'). Comment-stripping cannot help — it is markdown prose, not a comment. CLAUDE.md gate-writing bug (a): a gate that demands the deletion of the line explaining the defect is a gate that gets disabled. Exemption is declared HERE on the row, never in prose, so a future wave enforcing the contract cannot silently 'fix' it.

exempt_consumers.example: 10/s per UID and 3/s per IP on the place-order endpoint
exempt_consumers.why: A VENUE's API rate limit, not AlgoVault's free-tier quota. The pattern is written so these never match: it requires a digit adjacent to calls/day, so 'per IP' alone is inert. Asserted in both directions by the gate's self-test.

phrases.reason: Free tier is a monthly cap. Per-day phrasing overstates it.
